items.title: GB's men finish fourth World Gymnastics championships
paras: That meant they failed to qualify early for the Olympic Games in Los Angeles but will get another chance to reach the 2028 Games at next year's World Championships.

But the team, which included Courtney Tulloch, Joe Fraser, Jake Jarman, Harry Hepworth and Reuben Ward, finished with a total score of 247.395, behind Japan (251.928), Russia (250.329) and China (249.193). Joe Fraser, who will compete for the men's all-around title alongside team mate Jake Jarman, told BBC Sport that the team were "gutted now - but we come back stronger every time".

items.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
paras: India swung for the moon with Chandrayaan-1, its first deep space mission. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor.

Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov.

paras: His award-winning 55-year career as a grandmaster of the genre continues with his latest novel from Blackstone Publishing, " Lost on Paradise ", and we have an exclusive excerpt to share with our readers ahead of its release this week. He’s been a mainstay for go-to fantastic adventures featuring engaging characters, dynamic plotlines, and imaginative worlds for six decades.

The near-future, off-world escapades of "Lost On Paradise" are the latest addition to Foster’s acclaimed bounty of bestselling standalone novels and series, including the popular "Spellsinger" series. "Earth is crowded, polluted, and dismal," states the novel's synopsis.

items.title: Scientists Transplanted 306 Square Meters of Wild Salt Marsh Into The World's Largest Wave Machine And Let a S
paras: If we really want to know how our coastlines are going to fare under extreme conditions, we're going to need some extreme scientific experiments. Scientists from the Netherlands have raised the bar, going to great lengths to demonstrate the physical power of salt marshes in the face of massive storm surges.

Water engineer Pim Willemsen and his colleagues dug up 306 square meters of a real salt marsh from the coast of the Wadden Sea, and transplanted it into the world's largest wave generator, the Delta Flume . Then, they blasted the 'marsh' with a relentless series of storm waves for 21 hours.
